methodological_rigor.justification: The design is a retrospective biomarker study built from public transcriptomic datasets, single-cell analysis, WGCNA, multiple machine-learning models, external validation, Mendelian randomization, and a small in vitro validation arm. That is appropriate for hypothesis generation, but the model is selected after comparing many algorithms, there is no prospective validation, and the wet-lab work only tests one candidate gene. The analysis is extensive, yet it remains largely associative and does not convincingly rule out overfitting or multiplicity.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is best classified as an individual retrospective cohort/prediction-model study, so Oxford level 2b fits better than a purely exploratory design. The relevance score is high because the paper aims to stratify cervical cancer prognosis, examines immune and drug-sensitivity differences, and proposes HMGN1 as a therapeutic target. The patient impact is still unproven because the findings are retrospective and not tied to a prospective treatment decision.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the closest fit because the paper develops and validates a prognostic model using multiple cohorts. The manuscript does a good job of describing the data sources, feature selection, validation workflow, and companion wet-lab assays, which is stronger than a minimal biomarker paper. Public code is not visible in the blinded text, and the reporting stops short of clear calibration or decision-curve detail, so reproducibility is only moderate.

novelty_literature.justification: The study is novel in its combination of lactylation biology, single-cell analysis, machine-learning prognostic modeling, immune profiling, Mendelian randomization, and a focused HMGN1 validation in cervical cancer. That is a meaningful extension of the field, not a first-in-class discovery. At the same time, many components of the pipeline are established methods, so the novelty is cumulative rather than paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well structured, and the abstract is quantitatively grounded and broadly faithful to the reported workflow. The methods and results are dense but readable, and the narrative stays coherent across the computational and wet-lab components. Some claims are a bit stronger than the validation level warrants, but the presentation itself is clear.

key_strengths: Multiple public datasets plus an external validation cohort strengthen the prognostic model beyond a single-dataset study.
The paper links bioinformatics, immune analysis, Mendelian randomization, and in vitro validation in one coherent translational package.
The manuscript gives enough methodological detail to follow the feature selection and validation pipeline.
key_concerns: The model remains retrospective and is still vulnerable to overfitting despite the external validation set.
Public code is not visible in the blinded text, and the reporting does not show a full TRIPOD-level calibration/decision-analysis package.
The wet-lab validation is narrow and focuses on only one candidate gene.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a strong biomarker-development paper, but it is still a retrospective computational study with limited biological follow-up. Tier 3 is the safest plausible acceptance tier, with the work leaning toward minor rather than major revisions because the validation stack is broader than average.
